newsitem.title: USA: Dominion Resources profits top analyst forecast.
newsitem.headline: Dominion Resources profits top analyst forecast.

text.p: Dominion Resources Inc. reported a better-than-expected 13 percent rise in first-quarter profits to $169.9 million, including the utility's first earnings from a British power company it acquired earlier this year.

Dominion's net income, equivalent to 93 cents a share, compared with profits of $150.2 million, or 85 cents a share, in the first quarter of 1996. It easily beat the consensus Wall Street analyst forecast of 84 cents a share, according to First Call, which tracks analyst forecasts.
Revenues climbed by a third to $1.86 billion from $1.24 billion in the year-ago period, the Richmond, Va.-based company said.
Dominion Chairman Thomas Capps said profits were up despite an abnormally mild winter which cut earnings by the company's principal subsidiary, Virginia Power.
He attributed the higher profits to Dominion's diversification programme, which included the acquisition earlier this year of British power company East Midlands Electricty Plc.
Virginia Power earned $101.5 million from operations, compared with $147.4 million in the first quarter of 1996.

"The contrast between the two quarters is particularly notable when you recognise Virginia Power had extremely cold winter weather in 1996 to compare with the unseasonably mild temperatures this year," Capps said in a statement.
Nottingham, England-based East Midlands contributed $49.8 million in first-quarter operating earnings.
Dominion said East Midlands' earnings were unusually strong because only part of the quarter recognised the cost of debt associated with the acquistion, which was valued at $2.15 billion.

Among other subsidiaries, Dominion Energy -- which provides natural gas and sells electricity outside Virginia Power's traditional area -- earned $13.8 million from operations, compared with $5.9 million in the same period last year.
Dominion Capital, Dominion's financial services and real estate unit, had $8.9 million in operating earnings, compared with $2 million last year.
Dominion Resources stock rose 25 cents to $34.75 in consolidated afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
